summary: This class defines a decorated cookie as a special kind of Cookie, inheriting everything the base cookie already knows how to do and replacing only its description.

lines.text: The `extends` keyword makes DecoratedCookie a subclass of Cookie, so it automatically has the flavor field and every method Cookie provides.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so DecoratedCookie needs its own to accept the flavor when an object is created.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor, letting the parent class do the work of storing it. It must be the first statement in the constructor.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method from the parent class, so a typo in the method name becomes an error instead of a silent bug.
Redefining describe() with the same signature as in Cookie means calls on a DecoratedCookie object run this version instead of the inherited one.

lines.code: return "This " + getFlavor() + " cookie is decorated with sprinkles and icing!";
lines.text: The flavor is read through the inherited getFlavor() method because the field itself is private to Cookie, which is how subclasses reach a parent's data safely.
